failure_modes: Species/delivery barrier: Intranasal route fails to deliver intact EVs into CSF/olfactory‑adjacent tissues in the selected animal model (e.g., macaque‑like physiology), so in‑vivo recovery is negligible and any ex‑vivo PD (positive or negative) cannot be causally linked to intact‑EV exposure (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

Assay insensitivity/compatibility: Immuno‑capture reagents or spike‑in tracers perform poorly in low‑biomass lavage/CSF matrices (binding inhibited by buffers/devices or recovery below limit of detection), yielding false negatives for intact‑EV presence even when EVs are present (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Soluble co‑isolate confounding: Secreted soluble factors or non‑vesicular nanoparticles in conditioned medium reach CNS compartments and drive ex‑vivo cytokine modulation; particle‑count or capture signals (if any) correlate poorly with functional activity, causing misattribution of mechanism (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus).

Labeling/artifact bias: Spike‑in tracers or reporter labels alter EV pharmacokinetics or are released/degraded in vivo, so recovered signal reflects label fate rather than intact EV exposure (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

Inadequate membrane‑disruption control: Detergent/protease treatments incompletely distinguish membrane‑protected cargo from resistant soluble complexes or non‑vesicular particles, undermining the key discriminant between intact‑EV and non‑EV activity (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Low biomass sampling reproducibility: Small sample volumes and rapid clearance result in high variability and poor reproducibility of co‑localization metrics (particle peaks vs capture signals), making statistical linkage to ex‑vivo PD unmeasurable across replicates (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Manufacturing/processing damage: Downstream fractionation or formulation steps required to produce the ‘intact‑EV’ arm damage EV membranes or strip relevant surface markers (loss of capture epitopes), causing administered ‘intact’ material to be functionally altered and confounding attribution (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Translatability bias from rodents: Positive short‑interval rodent intranasal efficacy (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi) reflects rodent‑specific anatomy/clearance and does not predict detectability or mechanism in larger species, so the bridging experiment may be uninformative for clinical translation (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

Ex vivo assay non‑specificity: The microglia‑like cytokine readout responds to many perturbations (endotoxin carryover, detergent residues, or spike‑in contaminants), so observed cytokine modulation may not reflect intact‑EV delivered cargo (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Ethical/regulatory sampling limits: Short post‑dose sampling windows or invasive CSF/olfactory‑adjacent tissue collection may be ethically constrained in larger animals, forcing compromised timepoints or volumes that miss peak intact‑EV exposure and lead to false negatives (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).
strongest_objection: The single strongest, bounded reason the proposal could fail is that intranasally administered, membrane‑protected EVs are not present at measurable levels in the sampled CNS compartments (nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory‑adjacent tissue) in vivo — either because delivery is blocked in the chosen species/formulation or because the orthogonal capture/spike‑in assays lack sensitivity/compatibility in very low‑biomass matrices — producing a reproducible negative linkage between in‑vivo intact‑EV verification and ex‑vivo cytokine PD despite real therapeutic activity being mediated by soluble co‑isolates or by EVs undetectable with the chosen methods. This combines the delivery limitation observed in a large‑animal intranasal study with realistic assay/low‑biomass performance constraints and would lead to a false conclusion that intact EVs do not mediate short‑interval CNS effects.
